We also searched for genetic evidence to establish KIRREL3 as a risk factor for neurological disorders in large-scale studies on autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability (FDR < 0.1).

KIRREL3 deletions are a consistent feature of Jacobsen syndrome (chromosome 11q deletion syndrome), which typically results from large (7–20 Mb) terminal deletions at 11q23.3-qter that encompass KIRREL3 (11q24.2).
The syndrome’s characteristic intellectual disability appears specifically linked to loss of KIRREL3 gene.
This genotype–phenotype correlation strongly suggests KIRREL3 loss is the key contributor to cognitive impairment in Jacobsen syndrome.
